Standard financial-ratio ratings unfairly penalize nonprofits in high-need counties: the 0-10 standard rating is lower where county need is high.
Nonprofits in counties with higher poverty rates spend a smaller share of their expenses on programs.
Organizations in counties with a larger share of food-desert population rely more heavily on contributions, measured by revenue concentration.
Fundraising efficiency is lower in counties with higher unemployment rates.
Operating margins are thinner for nonprofits in counties with a higher housing burden.
